observation.visible_scene: High aerial (drone) view of a foggy coastal headland. A green, tree-covered peninsula occupies the lower-left to center, with a small group of white buildings at the bottom-left and a cluster of blue-roofed sheds plus a paved parking area at the center-right. Open water fills the upper portion of the frame, and thick white cloud/fog banks roll across the right side and over the water on the left.
visible_changes: The large white cloud mass on the right continuously deforms and billows, changing shape and brightness from frame to frame (e.g., its rounded bright core shifts and reshapes over the clip).
The thinner fog layer drifting over the water on the left slowly advances and recedes, altering the visible edge between water and mist.

The static terrain (headland, buildings, sheds, parking lot, far shoreline) remains fixed relative to one another but shifts slightly within the frame over time, indicating a slow camera drift/repositioning rather than object motion.
No editing cut or abrupt scene change is present; the sequence reads as one continuous shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause and direction of the wind driving the fog flow is not shown.
What lies beyond the upper water edge and below the bottom frame is unseen.
Whether the camera motion (and fog flow) continues, stops, or reverses after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact camera motion (slow pull-back vs. lateral drift/pan) is hard to confirm from background cues alone; only the net slight down-left shift of the static scene in the frame is clear.
It is difficult to fully separate the cloud's apparent translation from camera movement, though its shape change (deformation) is genuine independent motion.
The speed and direction of the fog flow are only loosely estimable from the sampled frames.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
